items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section VII, List of Answers on Topics 40:1
items.html: For at the time of the clothing of the lights in the vessels, whatever is coarser is regarded as more important and higher. The opposite is true after the departure of the lights from the vessels, for then whatever is coarser is lower. Therefore, since Da'at was the highest of all at the time of clothing, it is found to be the lowest of all at the time of departure. Hesed, whose coarseness is less than it, is higher than it; Gevura, whose coarseness is less than Hesed, is higher than Hesed; and Tifferet, whose coarseness is less than all of them, is higher than all of them. (p. 554, Item 19)
